summary: James Burnes worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1817 to 1820 and completed an LL.D. at the University of Glasgow by 1834.

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James C. Harle worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at Princeton (B.A. circa 1938–1942) and Oxford (B.A., D.Phil., D.Litt.), he was Assistant to the Dean at Princeton (1947–1949) and Keeper at the Ashmolean Museum (1967–1987).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He was Registrar at Calcutta High Court (1810), Principal of Hooghly Mohsin College (1839), and professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at EPHE under Bergaigne, Bréal, and Hauvette-Besnault. He directed EPHE in 1892 and was Professor of Persian Language and Literature at Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Drummond Anderson worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1875–1900), received his M.A. from the University of Cambridge by 1909, and became Cambridge's University Lecturer in Bengali in 1907.

James Duerlinger works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (circa 1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and was appointed Professor Emeritus at the University of Iowa in 1971.
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College from circa 1830 to 1833. He later held an academic post at Yale University from circa 1850 to 1892, where he taught Charles Rockwell Lanman.

James Fairbrother Edwards specialized in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Handsworth Theological College from circa 1904 to 1907 and served as Principal at the United Theological College, Pune, in 1930.

James Fergusson worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, having studied at the Royal High School. He became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society in 1840 and served as secretary to A. H. Layard at the Office of Works in 1868.

James Fieser works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University, and has held posts at the University of Tennessee at Martin (circa 1992) and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville.

James Fuller Blumhardt worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Lecturer in Bengali at the University of Cambridge (1883–1888), at University College London (circa 1896–1922), and worked at the British Museum from circa 1894 to 1921.

James G. Mullens specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Simon Fraser, Victoria, and McMaster universities, studying under Graeme MacQueen, Yün-hua Jan, and John G. Arapura, and took up a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Grant Liston Garthwaite worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Westminster College, London, served as a missionary and teacher with the Basel Mission (circa 1857–1860), and became a Fellow of the University of Madras in 1884.

James Grant Stephen specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from circa 1857 to 1861, earning a B.A., and served there as Lecturer in Hindustani between 1860 and 1863.

James Gray was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Akyab Government High School (1872), served as Professor of Pāli at Basic Education High School No. 1 Dagon, and was Professor of Pali at Rangoon University (circa 1884–1905).

James H. Austin, a neurologist working in Buddhist studies, trained under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the universities of Oregon and Colorado (emeritus professor 1967–1992), alongside appointments at Idaho, Florida, and Missouri.

James Hadley was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury. After tutoring at Middlebury College in 1845, he served as Assistant Professor at Yale University from 1845 to 1872.

James Hair Maclean worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the universities of Glasgow, Oxford, and Jena, and served as a missionary for the United Free Church of Scotland beginning in 1895.

James Haughton Woods specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Harvard, Episcopal Divinity School, Berlin, Oxford, and Strasbourg, learning from Lanman, Deussen, Venis, and Adkar. He served as professor at Harvard from 1913 to 1934.
